subject: POC success path & eval method alignment — NexisHealth
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@nexishealth.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@nexishealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC success path & eval method alignment — NexisHealth

Hi Lena / Tom,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good alignment on scope and the top success criteria. I wanted to capture the proposed success path and the two eval-method options we discussed so we can pick an approach and lock the schedule.

Quick recap (from the call):
- Goal: reduce triage false positives in clinical intake routing and improve first-touch classification accuracy for the 6 priority intents.
- Key constraints: PHI-sensitive data in messages, peak latency target for user-facing routing <= 200ms p95, and ability to audit decisions for compliance.

Two recommended evaluation tracks (please pick one, or we can do a hybrid):
1) Online shadowing (preferred if you want production-like behaviour)
   - Run Redwood model in shadow mode alongside prod traffic; we log decisions and metrics but do not route live traffic to model.
   - Pros: captures real distribution, latency, post-edit behavior.
   - Cons: needs tighter data handling (PII) and initial sampling to limit exposure.

2) Offline simulated evaluation (safe start)
   - Run batched inference against a labeled subset of historical events. Measure precision@k, recall, and micro-F1; simulate latency with replayed payloads.
   - Pros: fastest to run, minimal production footprint.
   - Cons: may miss live distribution shifts.

Proposed success criteria (we suggested on call):
- Functional: precision@1 >= 92% for priority intents, micro-F1 >= 0.88 on labeled set.
- Performance: p95 latency <= 200ms for online path; token-level cost target <= $0.003 per request (configurable).
- Operational: decision logs available for 30 days; no unredacted PHI written to long-term storage.

Suggested cadence & owners:
- Week 0 (this week): agree on eval method + sign MOU for POC scope (Owner: Sales / Tom to approve).
- Week 1: offline label validation + quick sim run (Owner: Marissa).
- Weeks 2–4: incremental online shadowing (1% -> 5% -> 10% traffic ramp) and monitoring (Owner: Marissa; Customer owner: Lena).
- End of Week 4: acceptance review + decision (go/no-go).

Attachments I attached: nexis-poc-success-metrics.xlsx (spreadsheet with metric definitions) and rdw-eval-rubric-v1.md (grading rubric).

Please confirm: which eval track do you want to start with? If shadowing, can you confirm acceptance of a limited-sampling ramp and provide the security contact so we can loop in our compliance team?

Next steps (proposed):
- You confirm eval method and security contact by Wed 10/7.
- We finalize POC kickoff date (we have availability the week of 10/12).

Thanks — looking forward to running this with you.

Best,
Karthik
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@nexishealth.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC success path & eval method alignment — NexisHealth

Karthik — thanks for the clear recap. Copying Tom.

We are leaning toward online shadowing because of the subtle differences in live traffic (bot noise, truncated messages, etc.). A couple of questions before we commit:
1) PII handling: can you guarantee that any PHI in shadow logs will be redacted before it leaves our VPC? We can provide a scrubbed sample feed, but we need to understand the options.
2) Sampling and ramp: could we do a shorter ramp (1% -> 3% -> 7%) and extend the shadow window to 6 weeks instead of 3 if that gives better statistical power?
3) SLA and rollback: if we see a spike in latency during shadowing, what are the immediate rollback/kill switches?

If you can answer the above and confirm a kickoff the week of 10/12, we can loop in our security team (attn: security@nexishealth.com).

Thanks,
Lena
Director, Clinical Operations — NexisHealth

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@nexishealth.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@nexishealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 14:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC success path & eval method alignment — NexisHealth

Thanks, Lena — great questions. I'm Marissa (Sales Engineer) — I'll own the setup and runbook with your team. Below is a pragmatic plan that balances safety and signal.

Recommended approach: hybrid (fast offline validation, then controlled shadow)
- Phase A (3 business days): offline simulated run against a 2k sample of historical records to validate labels and the rdw-eval-rubric metrics. Outcome: sanity-checks for precision@1 and micro-F1.
- Phase B (3 weeks nominal; flexible to 6 weeks): shadowing in your VPC. Start at 1% traffic for 3 days, then 3% for 1 week, then 7% for 2 weeks (we can extend weeks at your request). We can extend the total duration instead of pushing to 10% if you prefer slower ramping.

Privacy & security controls:
- Pre-filtering: we will run a local redaction step in your VPC; PII/PHI tokens are masked before any logs leave the VPC. We will only ship decision metadata + non-identifiable snippets unless you approve otherwise.
- Retention: decision logs retained in customer-controlled bucket for 7 days by default; option to increase to 30 days with a compliance addendum.
- Access: debug-level token traces require explicit approval; default run writes only decision IDs, scores, top-3 labels.

Instrumentation & acceptance signals:
- Metrics to collect: precision@1, recall@3, micro-F1, throughput, p50/p95 latency, top-class distribution shift.
- Acceptance rubric: pass if production-like shadow shows precision@1 >= 92% and no more than a 2x increase in p95 over baseline. See attached rdw-eval-rubric-v1.md for graded pass/fail/conditional criteria.

Schedule & owners (concrete):
- Wed 10/07: Security contact + sign MOU (Action: Lena).
- Mon 10/12: POC kickoff (Action: Marissa to schedule meeting + run initial offline batch).
- Week of 10/12: Phase A offline run complete (Action: Marissa).
- Weeks 10/19–11/02: Phase B shadow ramping (Action: Marissa + Lena).
- Target review: Fri 11/06 — acceptance meeting and exec summary (Action: Karthik).

Attachments: rdw-eval-rubric-v1.md (grading rubric) and nexis-poc-success-metrics.xlsx (metric definitions + sample dashboard). I uploaded the rubric to the Drive link earlier as well.

If privacy or retention limits are a blocker we can run the entire POC on a scrubbed dataset and do a longer offline run — that'll cost less integration effort but won't capture live latency.

I'll schedule the kickoff and include our cloud-security engineer for the redaction walkthrough.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference
